name: generalist-hub-first-source-registry
purpose: Use broad professional information platforms as the discovery entry layer so the Skill does not pre-commit to sectors. Specialist and official sources are validation/deep-dive layers only.

discoveryHubs.name: Wind Financial Terminal
strengths: global stocks, bonds, commodities, FX and macro coverage

discoveryHubs.name: iFinD
discoveryUse: candidate expansion from an initial event
doNotUseAs: independent origin when only mirroring third-party content

discoveryHubs.name: LSEG Workspace
strengths: Reuters News plus broad authoritative-source aggregation

discoveryHubs.name: AlphaSense
strengths: broad company filings, news, trade journals and research
semantic discovery across large document universe

discoveryRules: The weekly discovery process must begin from one or more generalist hubs, not from a predefined sector source list.

Discovery queries are cross-market and state-change oriented: surprise, shortage, inventory, price, order, utilization, backlog, export, margin, policy, capacity, default, tender, demand, supply, earnings revision, capital flow, regulation.
Sector assignment happens after event discovery, never before.
A hub result is a pointer, not proof. The underlying original source must be recovered whenever possible.
The same story mirrored across multiple hubs counts as one origin.
Hub disagreement is a feature: conflicting coverage triggers adversarial research rather than majority voting.
Specialist sources may generate a candidate only if the same candidate would survive a hub-agnostic event description; specialist feeds must not define the weekly universe.

validationLayers.purpose: quantify physical magnitude, persistence, breadth and causal mechanism
map event to listed-company earnings/cash sensitivity
measure what is already expected; later bullish research can be evidence of crowding

weeklyWorkflow: 1. Run broad event discovery across at least one China-centric hub and one global hub.
2. Cluster candidate events without assigning sectors first.
3. For each cluster, retrieve original source and timestamp.
4. Only then classify sector/value-chain and query relevant specialist/official validators.
5. Map direct A-share expressions using issuer/customer/supplier evidence.
6. Measure expectation, valuation and price absorption using hub consensus/research data.
8. Record misses: events later found from specialist/official sources that the hubs failed to surface.

experimentDesign.B: generalist hub-first discovery, same downstream V1.9 rules
experimentDesign.C: hub-first plus specialist/official validation, same selection rules
experimentDesign.D: C plus separately validated timing/absorption changes
experimentDesign.keyQuestion: Does hub-first discovery increase recall and sector diversity without lowering 60d excess-win rate?
